sections.h2: What does the Union County Register of Deeds do when you sell a house?
sections.html:
The Union County Register of Deeds is the office in Monroe that files your deed and the buyer's deed of trust so the sale becomes part of the public land record. Its own site describes a standardized, permanent record of real estate ownership and transfers in the county, and lists deeds, deeds of trust, cancellations, plats, assumed names and powers of attorney among the documents it records.

The same office handles birth, death and marriage records, marriage licenses, military discharges and notary commissions, and it works as a passport acceptance facility. For a seller, only the real estate side matters. Your closing attorney sends the signed deed here, and the recording date and time fix the buyer's place in line against anyone else claiming an interest in the parcel.

The county has been served by this office since the county was formed in 1842, according to the department page. An elected Register of Deeds runs it. Selling a Union County house for cash does not skip this step: even a quick sale ends with a recorded deed.

sections.h2: Who is allowed to give advice at the Union County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Nobody at the counter can advise you on the legal effect of a document. The county page says the office acts as a recording office only, and that North Carolina statutes bar the register and staff from practicing law.

In practice that means the staff will not supply legal forms, tell you how to fill one out, or explain what a filed instrument does to your rights. If you need a deed drafted, a name added or removed, or a question answered about title, the county tells visitors to consult an attorney. Most Union County sellers meet this early: a deed that changes who owns the house has to be a new deed, because the register will not edit an old one.

  • Adding or removing a name on title: record a new deed prepared by an attorney.
  • Questions about liens and judgments: the Clerk of Court's office at 704-698-3100, per the county FAQ.
  • Finding who owns a property by street address: the tax assessor at 704-283-3746, since the deed index is name based.

sections.h2: How do you record a deed in Union County, and when can you go?
sections.html:
You can record in person during office hours, Monday to Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., or send the document through an electronic recording vendor. The office is in the Union County Government Center at 500 North Main Street in Monroe, and the county FAQ places land records on the second floor.

For electronic filing the county names three vendors it currently uses: Simplifile, CSC and ePN. The FAQ says you contact those vendors directly to get set up, so a seller does not sign up with the county. Title companies and closing attorneys usually already have an account with one of them. If a buyer's lender is involved, ask the closing office which route it will use and when the recording confirmation will come back.

Paper filers should bring the original signed and acknowledged document and the payment for the fee. The statute that sets the fee says it is collected before filing, so a document without payment will not be accepted.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Union County?
sections.html:
The county's own FAQ prints a recording fee of $26.00 for the first fifteen pages and $4.00 for each page after that, in its answer about separation agreements, and the statewide schedule uses the same figures for instruments in general. Deeds of trust and mortgages carry a higher statewide fee. Ask the office for the current Union County fee sheet before you send a check.

Union County and statewide recording charges as printed by the county and the legislature
ItemCharge as printedSource
Deed or other instrument$26.00 first 15 pages, $4.00 each extra pageUnion County FAQ; G.S. 161-10
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 first 35 pages, $4.00 each extra pageG.S. 161-10
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trustNo feeG.S. 161-10
Plat$21.00 per sheetG.S. 161-10
Assumed name filing$26Union County FAQ
Excise tax on a deed, August 1, 1991 to present$2 per thousandUnion County FAQ

The statute calls its fees complete and exclusive, so the register cannot add other charges to a standard filing. A nonstandard document, such as one that does not meet the statute's layout rules, picks up an extra $25.00.

sections.h2: How does the transfer tax on a Union County deed work?
sections.html:
The deed excise tax is $2 per thousand dollars on deeds recorded from August 1, 1991 to the present, according to the Union County FAQ. The statute behind it puts the rate as $1.00 on each $500.00 or fractional part of the consideration or value, which is the same rate written another way.

The statute says the transferor, the person giving up the property, pays the tax to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded. In a normal sale that means the seller, and the charge usually shows on the settlement statement from the closing office. Half of the collected tax stays with the county general fund and half goes to the Department of Revenue, with the county allowed to keep a small share of the state half.

Do not guess the figure for your sale. The tax depends on the price or value stated in the deed, and the closing attorney will total it before closing.

sections.h2: What can you look up online for Union County land records?
sections.html:
The county website offers deeds back to 1973 and maps back to 1842. Anything older, and anything that is not a deed or plat, has to be searched in person.

The FAQ is blunt about two limits. The online look-up covers deeds and plats only, so no mortgage information appears there. And the land records system is name based, which means a search by street address will not work in the register's index.

  • Search by the owner's name, not by the address.
  • For a street address, call the tax assessor's office.
  • For mortgage and deed of trust details, visit the office or ask the closing attorney.
  • For neighborhood covenants, the FAQ says filed HOA documents, if they exist at the county, can be searched in the register's office.

Sellers use this record to confirm that the name on the deed matches the people signing, and that no unreleased deed of trust sits on the parcel.

sections.h2: Why does recording order matter on a Union County sale?
sections.html:
Under North Carolina law, a conveyance, lease of more than three years, option or right of first refusal is not good against lien creditors or buyers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies. Priority follows the order in which instruments are registered.

That is why attorneys record the deed quickly after closing and why a gap between signing and recording can matter. If an old deed of trust was never cancelled, the public index is what other parties will rely on. Satisfactions of deeds of trust record without a fee, so a paid-off lender has little reason to delay.

If you are selling a house with an old, unreleased lien, ask your closing attorney to check the index for it before the contract date, then confirm the release is recorded.

sections.h2: What other Union County offices touch a home sale?
sections.html:
Three offices come up most. The tax assessor at 704-283-3746 handles property addresses and ownership questions that the register's name-based index cannot. The Clerk of Court at 704-698-3100 holds liens and judgments, according to the county FAQ. The Register of Deeds is the third, for the deed itself.

The register also keeps notary commission records. A notary renewing a commission takes the oath at the office, and the FAQ lists a $10.00 fee for that. Ask your closing office to use a notary whose commission is current.

For a house with a probate, divorce or tax issue attached, those matters run through the courts and the tax office, not through the register. The register only records what those processes produce.

faqs.q: Is the Union County Register of Deeds open on weekdays only?
faqs.a: Yes. The county FAQ lists recording hours as Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Electronic filers using Simplifile, CSC or ePN can submit through those vendors, but confirm cutoff times with your vendor or closing office.

faqs.q: Can the Union County register help me write a deed?
faqs.a: No. The county says the office is a recording office only and staff cannot supply legal forms or tell you how to complete them. Use an attorney to draft the deed, then bring it to the office or have it filed electronically.

faqs.q: How much is the excise tax on a Union County deed?
faqs.a: The county FAQ prints $2 per thousand dollars for deeds from August 1, 1991 to the present. The statute states it as $1.00 per $500.00 or fractional part. The seller normally pays, and your closing attorney will total it for your deed.

faqs.q: Can I search Union County deeds by property address?
faqs.a: No. The register's land records are name based, and the website only carries deeds from 1973 and maps from 1842. For a street address, the county FAQ points you to the tax assessor at 704-283-3746.

faqs.q: Does recording a satisfaction of a deed of trust cost anything in Union County?
faqs.a: Statewide law lists no fee for recording satisfactions or cancellations of deeds of trust or mortgages. Ask the register's office to confirm for your filing before you send payment.
